concepts.description: The overall process by which cells extract energy from glucose and convert it into ATP, described in this document as a sequence of linked stages.
concepts.name: Cellular Respiration

concepts.description: The stage in which the electron transport chain uses electrons from NADH and FADH2 to drive ATP synthesis, producing the majority of the cell's ATP.
concepts.name: Oxidative Phosphorylation

concepts.description: A series of protein complexes on the inner mitochondrial membrane that pass electrons along and pump protons to build the gradient used for ATP production.
concepts.name: Electron Transport Chain

concepts.description: The mechanism by which the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane powers ATP synthesis during oxidative phosphorylation.
concepts.name: Chemiosmosis

concepts.description: The first stage of cellular respiration, in which glucose is broken down into pyruvate, yielding a small amount of ATP and NADH.
concepts.name: Glycolysis

concepts.description: A mitochondrial stage that oxidizes acetyl-CoA and generates additional NADH and FADH2 to feed the electron transport chain.
concepts.name: Citric Acid Cycle

concepts.description: Molecules that capture high-energy electrons released during glycolysis and the citric acid cycle and deliver them to the electron transport chain.
concepts.name: NADH and FADH2 Electron Carriers

concepts.description: The oxidation of pyruvate inside the mitochondrion to form acetyl-CoA, which links glycolysis to the citric acid cycle.
concepts.name: Acetyl-CoA Formation
